This year has officially become the year of the super app. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and has just admitted the app is "a bit of a mess." Now Microsoft CEO has also confirmed its Copilot super app is on the way.

Microsoft Copilot "super app" will integrate Cowork, chat, coding and more

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that combines Copilot chat, coding and intelligent agent features. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch this year, covering "consumer and commercial experiences." Nadella said: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat to Cowork to autopilot." He also said: "This quarter we will integrate these Copilot experiences, including coding capabilities, into a single super app... this is a significant step, and I look forward to sharing more details later."

OpenAI's launch of its own "super app" has turned into a mess. But that clearly hasn't stopped other companies from continuing with the super app approach.

Perhaps Microsoft can better deliver a multi-functional all-in-one app and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella has also recently said the company is gradually shifting from apps to focusing on developing intelligent agents. The AI era is still in its early stages, and the trends and best practices for building AI-centric user interfaces are still constantly evolving.

As for Apple, there are no signs of moving toward the super app direction, and it continues to launch standalone, specialised apps. Whether this strategy will change in the future remains to be seen.

What are your thoughts on the recent "super app" craze? Feel free to tell us in the comments section.
